Generally, the typical features of cathode limited cells can be seen i.e. a low-rate plateau as well as a power law-like decay of the capacity beyond a certain critical rate. The purpose of the ﬁt is to quantify the rate performance via the kinetic parameters Q , M α and n, which quantify the maximum value, onset of decay and decay slope of the capacity-R curve, respectively. The ﬁt results are plotted in Fig. 4. All parameter values and their dependencies are additionally shown in Table S2. QM is the maximum capacity value at the low-rate plateau and is in essence the extrapolated capacity obtainable from the cathode at inﬁnitely low rates (Fig. 4). QM is therefore suitable to quantify the AM utilization. In the case of ideal electronic percolation, one would expect that the QM value equals the nominal capacity of the AM. Measurements in reference LIBs resulted in 193 mAh g−1 for gran and 213 mAh g−1 for sc at 0.1 C, respectively. This discrepancy reﬂects intrinsic differences in the AMs which might come from differing production process or postproduction treatment by the suppliers.
